reconcile.note: Clarke merges the second-denial challengers into one continuous courtyard scene, so the crowd's charge in Matthew is simply echoed by the named relative in John.

discrepancy.note: Strauss finds the Evangelists agree only on the number three, diverging on the place, persons, and wording of each challenge to Peter.

quotes.text: In relation to the separate acts of denial, all the Evangelists agree in stating that there were three of them, in accordance with the prediction of Jesus; but in the description of the several instances they are at variance.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), on Matthew 26:73 and John 18:26.

sides.snippet: those who stood by came and said to Peter
sides.verseText: After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, \"Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.\"

sides.snippet: One of the servants of the high priest, being a relative of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said, \"Didn't I see you in the garden with him?\"
